passages.title: The Library That Never Closes
passages.text: In a small town in the south of Iraq, a group of university students has created an unusual library. It has no building, no opening hours and no librarian. Instead, the students built twelve wooden boxes and placed them in parks, cafés and bus stops around the town. Each box contains about thirty books, and anyone can take one for free, as long as they bring it back or leave another book in its place. The idea came from Noor, a literature student, who noticed that many teenagers in her town had never visited a bookshop. "Books are expensive, and the nearest real library is an hour away," she explains. At first, some people expected the books to disappear within days. In fact, the opposite happened: local residents started donating books, and the boxes are now fuller than when they began. The students are now planning to add a section for children's stories and are looking for volunteers to repair old books.

passages.title: Friends I Have Never Met
passages.text: When Ali was sixteen, he joined an online group for people who love astronomy. Most of the members were from other countries, and they communicated in English. At first, Ali only read their posts because he was worried about making mistakes. But one evening, someone asked a question about the moon that Ali could answer, so he decided to write a reply. To his surprise, several people thanked him and asked him more questions. Over the next three years, Ali became one of the most active members of the group. He improved his English, learned a lot about science and made friends in Brazil, Japan and Kenya. Last summer, he finally met one of them, a student from Nairobi, at a science conference in Turkey. "It felt strange," Ali says, "because I already knew him so well, but I had never heard his real voice." Ali now believes that the internet can bring people together, as long as they use it carefully.
